page: Microsoft Azure DC1s_v3 is a single-core virtual machine from the DCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 1 physical core and 1 thread, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reflect its single-core design. In single-core evaluations, the instance achieves average performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1875.88 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1628.0. Single-threaded compression tasks also perform in the average range, with gzip compression reaching 28.27 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound benchmarks are limited, falling into the lower percentiles. The multi-core Geekbench score is 1640.0, and the Passmark memory score is 994.05, with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured at 13.2 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC1s_v3 offers a dedicated, secure execution environment with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 at a low entry resource tier. This makes it suitable for lightweight workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation and moderate memory capacity without the overhead of multi-core architectures. Recommended workloads include basic single-threaded applications, lightweight database operations, simple web serving, and low-intensity background utility tasks.
